title: Volcan: hear your code review instead of scrubbing a diff

narration_audio.note: Filled in from the measured run. See video/README.md.

title_lines: Recorded from a local run of commit {sha7}.
outro_lines: Recorded from a local run of commit {sha7}. Public deployment pending.
Narration: synthetic ElevenLabs voice. Product speech: the browser's system voice.

beats.narration_text: This is the kind of patch an autonomous coding agent writes. A sighted reviewer scans it in seconds. A screen reader reads it one plus sign, one minus sign and one hunk header at a time, so the one line that flips an authorization check sounds like everything around it.
beats.speech_text: This is the kind of patch an autonomous coding agent writes. A sighted reviewer scans it in seconds. A screen reader reads it one plus sign, one minus sign, and one hunk header at a time, so the one line that flips an authorization check sounds like everything around it.
beats.visual_action: The companion page at first paint with the Inverted admin check preset, the label Simulated Alexa+ experience, not an Alexa skill, and GitHub write: dry-run. On the second sentence, Alt and 2 opens the patch box and shows the raw unified diff with its hunk header and plus and minus lines. No screen reader is recorded: headless capture has none.

beats.narration_text: This is Volcan, running locally on this machine. Before anything plays, the stage already shows the server's real answer for this patch, silently: the earcon's waveform with its falling pitch, the finding in words, and the Braille cells. One button plays it, pressed from the keyboard. Listen.

beats.product_sound_basis: Rehearsal on 2026-09-26 against the local server: 17.9 s from the Enter press to the browser's speech end event (earcon playing to ended 0.8 s, speech start to end 16.7 s), plus 2.1 s margin. video/capture-local.py fails the take if speech has not ended inside this window.
beats.visual_action: Scroll back to the stage: the silent preview with the waveform in its not yet heard colour, the Falling contour, the finding sentence, the Braille cells and the line Server's first sentence, not played yet. Alt and 1 focuses Hear this code review, then Enter after the narrator stops. The narrator is silent while the page plays the earcon WAV the server returned and the browser speaks the server's sentence, finding first, with the words lighting as the speech engine reports them.

beats.narration_text: The earcon came first, so the verdict arrived before the sentence. This patch touches security, so the cue falls; a clean patch gets a rising cue. The sentence opens with the finding itself. The engine meter reads local heuristic, because this run has no cloud credentials, and the round trip was measured in this browser.

beats.visual_action: Hold on the earcon caption and the spoken sentence, then open the information button beside Synthesis engine so the server's own reason for the local engine is on screen, with the measured round trip and the change size beside it.

beats.narration_text: Volcan's Model Context Protocol server is written by hand to revision 2025-11-25 over Streamable HTTP, with no SDK. This button runs a real initialize and a real tools list call, then prints the negotiated version, the session identifier from the response header, and the JSON Schema of all twelve tools.
beats.speech_text: Volcan's Model Context Protocol server is written by hand to revision twenty twenty-five, eleven, twenty-five, over Streamable H T T P, with no S D K. This button runs a real initialize and a real tools list call, then prints the negotiated version, the session identifier from the response header, and the Jason Schema of all twelve tools.
beats.visual_action: In Evidence, tab Server and MCP, press Run a real MCP handshake, hold on the four facts (2025-11-25, volcan-accessible-forge 0.1.0, the session id, 12 tools), then expand the first tool to show its published inputSchema.

beats.narration_text: A high-consequence command is staged behind a single-use grant, bound by HMAC-SHA256 to its payload hash and to a lease. A human presents the grant, and the server answers: accepted, released to you, nothing run. The plan, git diff HEAD, stays a plan. No file under src imports subprocess, and a test walks every module's syntax tree to keep it that way.

beats.visual_action: In Evidence, select the Governed actions tab, press Stage an action and hold on the lease countdown, then press Approve with the grant and hold on GRANT ACCEPTED, the Outcome row released to you, nothing run, the line Dry run only, nothing was executed, and the audit row.

beats.narration_text: On this commit, 572 automated tests pass, and 22 of 22 protocol conformance checks pass against this server. There is no Alexa skill yet, the public endpoint runs an older commit, and this run called no Bedrock model. The page says so on screen. Volcan is for the developer who reviews code by ear and by touch.

Close on the page heading and the Simulated Alexa+ experience label.
